# Project: Air Fryer Toolkit (`airfryertoolkit/`)

**What:** airfryertoolkit.com is a set of niche air-fryer conversion calculators. The engine is the
product: food-type multipliers, basket vs oven-style airflow, a model max-temp ceiling (time is
added back when the temperature is clamped), and °F/°C/gas mark.
**Stack:** Astro 6 with `output: 'server'` and prerendered pages, `@astrojs/cloudflare`, a
Cloudflare Worker with static assets, Tailwind CSS 4.
**Locales:** en (root, unprefixed), es, pt, fr, de, set by `i18n` in `astro.config.mjs`.
**Branch:** `main`.

## Read first, every session
1. `competitor-analysis.md` (local only): **Section 0** (build guide and non-negotiables),
   **Section 6** (definition of done) and **Section 10** (prompt queue: 10.0 is the current
   prompt, 10.1 is the shipped log). Read the prompt from the line the owner names.
2. `DESIGN.md` for visual decisions.

## Commands
```
npm run dev          # astro dev
npm run check        # astro check — must be 0 errors
npm run build        # content-dates.mjs → astro build → check-sitemap.mjs (fails on a bad sitemap)
npm run test:e2e     # full Playwright suite
npm run test:urls    # builds, serves under wrangler dev, checks every sitemap URL: 200 + self-canonical
npm run indexnow     # submits every live sitemap URL to IndexNow
```
**Gate before any push:** `npm run check` → `npm run build` → `npm run test:e2e` →
`npm run test:urls`. Report all four counts. `npm run build` regenerates
`src/data/content-dates.json`, so commit it.

## Shipping (the owner's exact procedure)
1. Commit all changes (common §2), then `git push origin main`.
2. **Cloudflare Workers Builds deploys automatically from GitHub.** Pushing *is* the deploy.
3. Wait until the changed and new URLs return 200 on `https://airfryertoolkit.com` (poll with curl).
4. `npm run indexnow` and report how many URLs went out.
5. If the prompt asks, resubmit the sitemap in Search Console (owner's Chrome).

**Don't run `npm run deploy` or `wrangler deploy` by default**, and never present or "activate"
the `*.workers.dev` link. The owner said: "don't activate the worker link, just follow the settings
and rules added in this project". Use a manual wrangler deploy only if the owner asks for one, or
if the GitHub build is confirmed broken and the owner agrees. Don't touch `workers_dev`,
routes or bindings in `wrangler.toml` without being asked.

## Non-negotiable build rules
- **Engine/data:** all conversion math lives in `src/lib/converter.ts`, with no second copy of
  any multiplier and no arithmetic in components. Times and temps live only in
  `src/data/presets.ts`, which holds numbers only (`slug, category, engine{kind,food}, tempF,
  minutes, flipAt?, shakes?, internalF?, internalAlt?, doneBy?, sizes[]`). Oven and fan
  equivalents are derived in `src/lib/presets.ts`, never stored. Sourced data (preheat, model
  max temps) carries its source and the manual page in the data file.
- **Every number in copy is a `{KEY}` placeholder** filled from the engine by
  `fillPlaceholders`. The typed-number test covers every dictionary. A page's own temperature
  inside its question text may stay typed.
- **UI:** live output on every keystroke, never a Calculate button. No emoji (SVG geometric
  marks only). Terracotta `#ee884f` accent only. Colors come only from `global.css` tokens. No
  email gate on the printable chart. No popups.
- **Widgets:** one forward widget (`ConverterWidget.astro`, `source` prop) and one reverse widget
  (`ReverseConverterWidget.astro`, `target` prop) serve every direction. Add a mode to them and
  never clone a widget.
- **Content:** 500–600 words (German pages ≥510). Every page needs a distinct failure mode and
  worked example, 5–6 FAQs, and an internal-temp target for every protein (165°F poultry, 145°F
  fish, steak and chops). No recipes, food photos or affiliate roundups. Run the overlap watch on
  sibling pages: each must lead with a different *cause*.
- **JSON-LD:** WebApplication + FAQPage (+ BreadcrumbList), always `is:inline`. The FAQ uses the
  shared `<details>` component, and answers are in the server-rendered HTML.

## i18n: every new page ships in all 5 languages, in this order
1. Use the same slug in every locale (no translated slugs).
2. Extend `Dictionary` in `src/i18n/types.ts`.
3. Write en, then real es/pt/fr/de copy. Never placeholder or machine-stub text.
4. Prose goes in dictionaries (`src/i18n/dictionaries/…`, including `presets/`, `brands/` and
   the per-family folders) keyed by slug. Never put English prose in data files.
5. Build one shared `{Name}Body.astro` with a `locale` prop. Never duplicate markup per language.
6. Add `src/pages/{slug}.astro` plus thin wrappers in `src/pages/{es,pt,fr,de}/`.
7. Pass `locale` and `translatedSlug` to `<Layout>` and `<SiteNav>`, and `locale` to widgets.
8. Data-driven families (temperature landings, °C landings, presets) use one dynamic route
   over one exported array, one copy file per locale, and `{KEY}` placeholders.
9. Build every internal link with `localizedPath` / `localizedUrl`. Never hand-type `/${locale}/`.

## Sitemap and homepage wiring (`src/site.config.ts`)
- 5-locale page: add it to **`TRANSLATED_PAGES`** (emits 5 `<url>`s with reciprocal hreflang).
- English-only page: add a row to **`STATIC_PAGES`** in `src/pages/sitemap.xml.ts` (about,
  contact, privacy-policy, terms, and English-first brand pages). Never put a page in both lists.
- Add the slug to **`LIVE_PAGES`**. That flips homepage cards and cross-links from "Coming soon"
  to live. English-only pages use the `locales` field, and their translated cards stay
  "Coming soon".
- Add new routes to `scripts/content-dates.mjs` (sitemap lastmod). A missing entry broke the
  live sitemap once.
- `siteConfig.tools` is dead code. Never recreate `public/sitemap.xml`.
- URL form: no trailing slash, and locale roots are `/de`, not `/de/`. The setup is
  `trailingSlash: 'never'` + `build.format: 'file'` + `html_handling = "drop-trailing-slash"` +
  `public/_redirects` (`/*/ → /:splat 308`).

## Local-only here
`competitor-analysis.md`, `manuals/` (Ninja/Cosori/Philips owner's guides, kept so values can be
re-read), `.dev.vars`, `.agents/`.

## 2. Permission to act: commit, push, deploy

- **Never commit, push or deploy unless the owner asks** in this conversation ("commit",
  "push", "deploy", "ship it"). Finish the work, report it, and stop.
- "commit" means **stage every change in the repo**, including files left over from earlier
  sessions (the owner often continues across sessions). Run `git status` first. Leave out only
  the local-only files in §3. After `git add -A`, run `git status` again and unstage anything
  from §3 before committing.
- "push, commit and deploy" (or "deploy") means: commit → push → ship the way the table in §1
  says → confirm it is live → **IndexNow** (tool sites). IndexNow is part of every deploy by
  default; never ask about it.
- Keep unrelated changes in **separate commits** (e.g. a `.gitattributes` change gets its own
  one-line commit and does not go into a feature diff).
- Commit messages: one plain sentence saying what changed for the user, such as
  `Fix °C landing routes, breadcrumbs and sitemap dates`. No "WIP" and no "update files".
- Never force-push, `git reset --hard`, `git clean`, rewrite history, or delete branches unless
  the owner asks for that exact action.
- Before you say "pushed", check that it worked: `git status` shows nothing to commit and
  `git log origin/<branch> -1` matches your commit. If one file was left out, say so (this has
  happened before: "one file is still not committed and pushed").

## 5. Verification and reporting

- **Nothing counts as "passed" without a number.** Report the counts, for example
  "astro check 0 errors · build OK · e2e 612 passed, 1 skipped · test:urls 410 passed".
- Run the project's full gate before any push (each project section lists it). If a test fails,
  report the output. Never weaken or delete a test to make it pass.
- Add tests that would have caught the bug you fixed (sitemap parses, every URL returns 200,
  canonicals point to themselves, engine numbers come from the engine).
- After a deploy, **check the live site**: `curl -sI` the changed URLs (200, no redirect chain),
  check that `sitemap.xml` parses, and check the new pages are in the sitemap. Then run IndexNow
  and report how many URLs it submitted.
- Don't state search results, rankings or traffic you haven't fetched. Rankings come **only from
  Search Console**. Only cite numbers you have read in an official source. If you can't verify
  a value, say so. Don't invent one.
- If an action is blocked (by a permission prompt, the classifier or a missing login), say
  exactly which command was blocked and why. Don't claim it ran.

## 7. Windows machine gotchas (cost real time before)

- The path contains a space: always quote `"D:\Part time\SaaS\..."` (Git Bash:
  `"/d/Part time/SaaS/..."`).
- **`git` says "dubious ownership"** in `quickmeasuretool` / `portfolio` because the folders were
  moved from `D:\SaaS`. The owner fixes this once, by running
  `git config --global --add safe.directory "D:/Part time/SaaS/<project>"`. For a read-only check
  you can use `git -c safe.directory="*" ...`.
- Stopping `wrangler dev` leaves `workerd.exe` and wrangler `node` processes alive. They lock
  `dist/`, and the next `astro build` fails with a misleading "options.recursive is no longer
  supported" error. Kill them first:
  `Get-Process workerd -EA SilentlyContinue | Stop-Process -Force`, plus any node process whose
  command line contains `wrangler`.
- `astro build` sometimes prints "Complete!" and then a libuv `UV_HANDLE_CLOSING` assertion.
  The build still succeeded, so rerun only the step after it.
- Memory is tight. Claude Code may kill an idle dev server or test run with a "low memory" note.
  Don't restart it on your own; report it. Run one Playwright suite at a time.
- Astro 6 + `@tailwindcss/vite`: pin `"vite": "^7.3.2"` (and `tailwindcss` /
  `@tailwindcss/vite` `4.3.0`) or npm pulls vite 8 and the build breaks.
- `npx wrangler types` crashes on this machine. Bindings are declared by hand in `env.d.ts`.

## 8. Content and SEO rules shared by the tool sites

- Every page passes `title`, `description` and `canonical` to `<Layout>`. Tool pages also carry
  **WebApplication + FAQPage** JSON-LD (BreadcrumbList where the project uses it), using
  `<script type="application/ld+json" is:inline>`.
- Canonical URLs have **no trailing slash**. The slashed form must return exactly one 301/308,
  never a 307 or a chain.
- The sitemap is **generated** (`src/pages/sitemap.xml.ts`). Never create a static
  `public/sitemap.xml`. After adding pages, resubmit the sitemap in Search Console when asked.
- Thin-content guardrail: 500–600 words per page minimum, with a distinct worked example, a
  distinct FAQ, and a real reason for the page to exist. **Overlap check first:** grep for the
  target keyword. If an existing page already answers it, expand that page instead of adding a URL.
- No emoji in the UI (SVG marks only). No interstitials or newsletter popups. Ads only in dead
  zones, never over or above the tool. `<AdSlot>` handles its own "no ads yet" guard.
- Mobile: test at 375px and 412–430px, with tap targets of 44px or more.
- When you change a backend (email, storage, third-party service), grep the whole repo for the
  old name. Privacy and terms pages describe implementation details and go stale without
  warning.
